ShroudMap keeps per-cell player masks (ClearMask/FogMask, derived, not saved) so ObjectShroudSystem computes every player's getShroudedStatus with AND/OR over the object's cells. Queries walk only the archetypes in use (the registry keeps them in signature order, so chunk order is unchanged) and keep their prepared chunks until a chunk-layout event names an archetype they match; archetype matching is lazy per creation index (a long game leaves ~1500 archetypes, ~115 in use); Archetype::Has/ColumnIndex are one dense lookup (world.Get). Job system: a batch completes when its jobs are done (a pending count), not when every worker has checked in; workers announce themselves (inside count) and keep out of a closed batch, so a worker the OS has not scheduled no longer holds a wave for a time slice (the ~16 ms spikes); jobs queued for it are taken by the caller. Spatial/collider index rebuild: stable radix sort of packed (cell, entity index) keys in reused buffers. VictorySystem: standing worked out per chunk (no role: chunk skipped; dying/inactive/under construction per chunk); the owned list is only sorted when a player falls. UInt128: hardware 64x64 multiply at run time, std::bit_width, exact integer-Newton square root for 64-bit values. ShroudMap discs: the operation chosen once per disc, row runs walked by pointer, scanline buffers reused. Soak: SOAK_SPIKES=<ms> breaks every slow tick down by part and system. Routes: the A* keeps each cell's search state in one record, carries cell coordinates in its open-set entries, reads the eight neighbours' openness once, and orders its open set by packed (f, h, cell) keys in a 4-ary heap when they fit 64 bits (the same total order: the same routes). RouteRequestSystem gathers the tick's requests in chunk/row order and plans them spread over the pool (a batch system borrowing the jobs through the new ecs::JobPool resource the scheduler sets; a scratch per job), writing routes back in request order. Path zones (clientSafeQuickDoesPathExist's zone map): without decks the flood fill runs over a byte table of the usable cells with plain index steps (no division per cell), visiting in the same order, so the zone numbers are the same; the ground's types are read once in index order. Path zones without decks are now labelled by runs: each row's usable cells form runs, joined to the overlapping runs of the row above by union-find, and numbered in the order each zone's first run comes, which is the flood fill's numbering (cross-checked equal on the soak's maps); a rebuild after an obstacle change costs ~0.1 ms instead of ~1 ms. Zone rebuild without decks: both zone maps' usable cells in one pass over the grid's own type array (NavigationGrid::Types) into buffers kept with the plane, then run labelling that skips eight cells at a time over whole open or closed stretches: ~0.2 ms for 140k cells (was ~1 ms); the same numbers. ECS archetype graph edges: an archetype remembers where adding or removing a component leads, so World::Add/Remove (object creation adds dozens) skip building and looking up the signature (the same archetypes, made in the same order). Row pieces: a system whose rows are independent may declare SystemTraits PieceRows; its query then prepares large chunks as pieces of that many rows (each its own logical chunk: outputs and commands in row order), so the scheduler can share a heavy system out (minefields, object shroud, targeting, movement, spatial/collider index, appearance, crush, guards, area presence, contacts, weapons, snapshot). MinefieldSystem is now chunk-parallel: its shots gathered per chunk (MineShots) and queued in chunk order after the chunks, as its one-pass version queued them.
